title: Sparse top-k Mirror LoRA atoms
hypothesis: A small bank of shared low-rank update atoms plus sparse task codes can reconstruct multiple LoRA functions at lower actual bytes and active adapter compute than storing each task delta independently.
mirror_coordinate: sparse top-2 atom indices and coefficients per task
controls: MoLE-style direct top-2 mixture of the same shared atoms
shared atom bank with dense coefficients
task: Synthetic matrix-delta bank: discover a rank-6 shared atom span on development task identities, encode fresh low-rank compositions, and measure heldout matrix reconstruction, serialized bytes, active atoms and compute proxy.

development.selection_metric: Fit rank-6 shared span from development task matrices; rank and top-k frozen at 6 and 2.

fresh.split: Each world uses 12 development tasks to fit the shared basis, then 12 in-span and 4 out-of-span fresh task matrices. Fresh identities are disjoint; oracle matrix coding is evaluated separately from learning m from examples.

success_gate: On >=2/3 worlds, in-span reconstruction MSE <=1e-8 and shared atom bank actual bytes <=60% of full delta bank, with top-2 active atoms; Mirror-specific value also requires a quality/storage/active-compute advantage over matched MoLE-style direct atom mixing.
failure_gate: FAIL if in-span quality or storage gate fails on >=2/3 worlds, or if direct MoLE-style mixing matches Mirror on the Pareto axes. Out-of-span failures and private-residual costs must be reported.
boundaries: atoms are aligned to the synthetic generative family
fresh task code is oracle-fit from full delta matrices, not learned from examples
no pretrained model or end-to-end adapter training claim
LoRA gauge invariance is addressed by comparing full functional delta matrices, not raw factor coordinates
